name: Agentic Research Platform
tagline: Agent pipeline that plans, authors, validates and publishes B2B and B2C surveys to Qualtrics.
problem: Writing a research survey means turning a vague goal into sections, question types, scales and compliance checks, then rebuilding it by hand in Qualtrics. Research teams repeat this for every study and reuse their old question banks inconsistently. The platform takes a goal and audience and walks it through planning, authoring, validation and publishing using the team's own question banks as reference.
how: Upload question banks, templates, policy documents and past surveys into a corpus, where they are chunked and embedded.
Describe the research goal, audience (B2C, B2B, minors or mixed), and topics that must be included.
The Planner agent turns that into a JSON survey spec with sections, scale policy, logic policy, length budget and language policy.
The Author agent writes questions per section, using a four-stage retrieval over the corpus (filter, semantic rerank, diversity, policy veto) for reference questions.
The Validator agent runs rule-based checks on scales, types, duplicates, leading words, compliance, length and required items, then an LLM pass that scores clarity and neutrality.
The Publisher agent maps questions to Qualtrics question types, builds blocks and flow, and activates the survey; the wizard also exports JSON, CSV or Markdown.
features: Six-step wizard: Welcome, Knowledge Base, Plan, Review, Validate, Export.
Classic tabbed UI with Survey Planner, Question Author, Validator, Model Browser and Document Upload.
Model registry of 19 paid and open-source models with provider, supported tasks and quality score, filterable by type.
Rule-based checks for leading or prescriptive wording, duplicate questions (similarity threshold 0.90), scale and type mismatches, and survey length limits.
Support in the spec for MaxDiff, CBC, Gabor-Granger and Van Westendorp pricing methods.
Qualtrics publishing through the Qualtrics API.
SQLite mode with no Docker or PostgreSQL, plus a PostgreSQL and pgvector setup.
ai: Planner agent prompts an LLM (GPT-4 Turbo by default) to produce a structured survey specification as JSON.
Author agent prompts an LLM to write question stems and options per section, grounded in retrieved chunks from the corpus.
Validator agent asks an LLM to score each question for clarity, neutrality, redundancy and coverage on a 1 to 5 scale.
OpenAI embeddings (text-embedding-3-small) index the uploaded corpus for retrieval.
A model manager routes tasks to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or open-source models via Ollama or vLLM.

stack.frontend: Static HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript (wizard and classic UI)
stack.ai: OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs, OpenAI embeddings, optional Ollama or vLLM
stack.deploy: Docker Compose, Gitpod, Railway or Render guides

screens.title: Welcome
screens.caption: The wizard landing page lays out the six-step journey from uploading knowledge to exporting a survey. The badge at the top shows the API health check.

screens.title: Knowledge base
screens.caption: Pick a document type and audience and attach files, here the repo's sample B2C question bank, to add to the corpus the Author agent retrieves from.

screens.title: Plan survey
screens.caption: Enter the research goal, target audience, model tier and must-include topics. Submitting sends this to the Planner agent.

screens.title: Validate
screens.caption: The validation step lists what gets checked: clarity, leading questions, length and respondent fatigue, GDPR and compliance, and question flow.

screens.title: Export
screens.caption: The final step downloads the validated survey as JSON, CSV or Markdown.

screens.title: Classic UI: Survey Planner
screens.caption: The tabbed classic interface exposes each agent separately. The planner form takes a goal, audience, required topics and model type.

screens.title: Question Author
screens.caption: Generate a set number of questions of a chosen type, such as Likert scale, for a single topic.

screens.title: Model registry
screens.caption: Browse the models seeded into the registry, with provider, paid or open-source type and quality score.

screens.title: Open-source models
screens.caption: Filtering by type shows the open-source options, such as Llama 3.1 70B and Qwen 2.5 72B via Ollama.

screens.title: Upload documents
screens.caption: The classic upload tab adds question banks and templates to the knowledge base and lists what has been uploaded.

screens.title: API reference
screens.caption: The FastAPI Swagger page lists the corpus, survey, study, agent and model endpoints the UI calls.

run:
python setup_sqlite.py  # creates venv, installs packages, writes .env with DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///./survey_data.db, creates tables, seeds the model registry
bash start_app.sh  # starts the FastAPI backend on :8000 and the frontend UI on :3000
notes: Ran locally with SQLite: FastAPI backend from backend/ and the static frontend served with python -m http.server. Installed the minimal package list from setup_sqlite.py plus numpy and tenacity, created tables and seeded the model registry the same way the setup script does. Local-only changes: pointed the frontend API base URL at the capture port, and fixed the /health check to wrap SELECT 1 in sqlalchemy text() so it works on SQLAlchemy 2 (without it the status badge shows Error). No LLM API key was available and the repo has no mock mode, so the Planner, Author and LLM validation steps were not run and no generated survey is shown; corpus upload also needs OpenAI embeddings, so files were selected but not submitted. The Review, Validate and Export wizard steps are shown in their empty state, reached by calling the wizard's own goToStep function since the UI only advances after a plan is generated. The model browser and API docs show real data from the running backend. The task filter in the model browser returns nothing because it reads a field the registry does not return, and model cards show an 'undefined' task badge for the same reason.
